create.name: Satish Kumar
create.bio:
Satish Kumar left home at the age of nine to become a wandering Jain monk, and at eighteen, moved by Gandhi's example, he returned to ordinary life to work for peace. In his twenties he walked from India to Moscow, Paris, London and on to America without carrying any money, relying on strangers for food and shelter, and carried a gift of 'peace tea' to each of the nuclear powers' heads of government. That pilgrimage, and the trust in others it asked of him, still runs through everything he teaches.

He went on to found the Resurgence Trust, an educational charity, and for more than four decades edited its magazine, now Resurgence & Ecologist, where he remains Editor Emeritus. He also co-founded Schumacher College in Devon and still teaches there as President Emeritus. His talks, workshops and books join spiritual practice with care for the living world, under themes he calls reverential ecology, voluntary simplicity, holistic education and peace. Among his books are the memoir No Destination, Soil, Soul, Society, which sets out his trinity of earth, inner life and community, and Radical Love. He was given the Goi Peace Award in 2022.

books.title: Radical Love: From Separation to Connection with the Earth, Each Other, and Ourselves
books.author: Satish Kumar
books.description: Short chapters of practical advice on living with love towards the earth, other people and oneself. Kumar draws on his years as a parent, campaigner and teacher to suggest how a time of crisis and scarcity might be met with harmony and generosity instead.

books.title: Soil, Soul, Society: A New Trinity for Our Time
books.author: Satish Kumar
books.description: Kumar's best-known statement of his outlook, first published in Britain and later issued in a US edition. It argues that care for the land, for our inner life and for one another belong together and cannot be pursued apart.

free_resources.title: Change the Story: short films with Satish Kumar
free_resources.description: A series of brief films, each around two minutes long, in which Kumar offers a reflection on one theme from his teaching. The full set can be watched free online.
